meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, я за ними ухаживаю.
examples.trans: Thank you, I take good care of them.

examples.text: Спасибо за приглашение, я обязательно приду.
examples.trans: Thank you for the invitation, I will definitely come.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know'.

examples.text: Я знаю, что вам нельзя работать.
examples.trans: I know that you must not work.

examples.text: Откуда я знал, что Елена нас слышит?
examples.trans: How was I supposed to know that Elena could hear us?

examples.text: Кстати, познакомьтесь, это мой муж Николай.
examples.trans: By the way, meet my husband Nikolai.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лёва, какую ерунду ты сейчас говоришь?
examples.trans: Lyova, what nonsense are you talking right now?

examples.text: Странные какие-то отношения у вас двоих.
examples.trans: The two of you have a rather strange relationship.

examples.text: Как можно было сказать, что я болею?
examples.trans: How could you blurt out that I am sick?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Как можно было сказать, что я болею?
examples.trans: How could you blurt out that I am sick?

examples.text: Леночка сказала, что вы угостите нас обедом.
examples.trans: Lenochka said that you would treat us to lunch.

examples.text: Аня мне сказала, что тебе очень идёт.
examples.trans: Anya told me that it suits you very well.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'let's go', paired with 'идти'.

examples.text: Завтра пойдёшь к врачу в два.
examples.trans: Tomorrow you are going to the doctor at two.

examples.text: Может, пойдёшь сегодня вечером с нами?
examples.trans: Maybe you will come out with us tonight?

examples.text: Ладно, я тогда пойду, не буду мешать.
examples.trans: Alright, I will go then, I will not bother you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.text: Всё хорошо, мы уже скоро поедем.
examples.trans: Everything is fine, we will be going soon.

examples.text: Конечно, пойдём скорее садиться в машину.
examples.trans: Of course, let us go get in the car quickly.

examples.text: Очень жалко, что он скоро умрёт.
examples.trans: It is a great pity that he will die soon.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Поставь телефон на громкую связь.
examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

examples.text: Вы лучше спокойно дома отдохните.
examples.trans: You had better rest quietly at home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'home', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы лучше спокойно дома отдохните.
examples.trans: You had better rest quietly at home.

examples.text: Хорошо тебя дома родители воспитали.
examples.trans: Your parents raised you well at home.

examples.text: Я ещё хочу проводить Катю домой.
examples.trans: I still want to walk Katya home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'for now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы лучше спокойно дома отдохните.
examples.trans: You had better rest quietly at home.

examples.text: Вообще-то мы хотели спокойно посидеть девочками.
examples.trans: Actually we wanted to sit quietly with the girls.

examples.text: Возьми его себе, я пока не хочу.
examples.trans: Take it for yourself, I do not want it yet.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'left, departed', paired with 'уезжать'.

examples.text: Пойдём скорее ко мне домой, пока мама уехала.
examples.trans: Let us go quickly to my place while mom is away.

examples.text: Да, моя мама уже уехала на дачу.
examples.trans: Yes, my mom has already left for the dacha.

examples.text: Я уеду на час.
examples.trans: I'll be gone for an hour.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'kissed'.

examples.text: Они долго целовались.
examples.trans: They were kissing for a long time.

examples.text: Ты вчера целовался с моей девушкой!
examples.trans: Yesterday you kissed my girl!

examples.text: Вы целовались прямо в ресторане!
examples.trans: You were kissing right in the restaurant!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Понимаешь, Лёва, тут дело очень тонкое.
examples.trans: You understand, Lyova, this is a very delicate matter.

examples.text: А у вас тут закрытая вечеринка?
examples.trans: Are you having a private party here?

examples.text: Он целовался тут у лифта!
examples.trans: He was kissing right here by the elevator!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Поставь телефон на громкую связь.
examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'elevator' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он целовался тут у лифта!
examples.trans: He was kissing right here by the elevator!

examples.text: А кто тогда целовался около лифта с сотрудницей?
examples.trans: Then who was kissing a female employee near the elevator?
